text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired for service `redis-acceptqueue` (sev: high) — 80% accept queue, 95th latency ~450ms, error rate spike

pagerduty: PagerDuty autogenerated: Alert #PD-3198 -> paging oncall (priority: P1). Escalation -> ops-sre.

alex_chung: ACK. I'm checking accept-queue and client counts now.

maria_g: seeing a steady increase in `redis.accept_queue_length` and `netty.queue_wait` across api-prod and batch-prod fleets. P95 token-generation latency climbing. Noticed a correlation with a customer traffic ramp from EU region.

kevin-w: any PG impact too or only redis?

maria_g: currently mainly redis. Postgres connections ok but a couple of pgbouncer queues are growing for async jobs.

alex_chung: running checks:
```
# redis: client list and slowlog head
redis-cli -h redis-primary-prod CLIENT LIST | wc -l
redis-cli -h redis-primary-prod SLOWLOG GET 5

# pgbouncer: stats
psql -h pgbouncer -c "SHOW POOLS;"
```

alex_chung: quick outputs: CLIENT LIST = 12500 (maxclients 13000), accept_queue ~ 640, slowlog shows short burst of commands > 1000ms.

raj_patel: ops-sre: can we enable acceptqueue backpressure mitigation? Suggest temporarily increasing `maxclients` by 10% on affected nodes and routing non-critical traffic to fallback model variants (low-cost/readonly).

ops-sre: starting rolling config bump on cluster shard a-c (5 nodes). Will also disable a noisy batch worker pool if needed.

support-bot: incoming CS tickets: ~12 reports of generation timeouts and 2 customers with errors 503. Severity customer-impact: degraded for heavy-gen customers in EU region.

maria_g: initiating traffic steering to EU region fallback: switch route policy to `prefer-dedicated-fallback` for model-gen endpoints for 10m. This should lower peak by ~30%.

alex_chung: applied routing change, monitoring. Latency P95 dropped to ~260ms within 90s. Accept_queue down to ~320.

incident-bot: Note added: runbook link https://redwood-internal/runbooks/redis-acceptqueue. Playbook step 2: scale up redis ephemeral nodes OR enable client backoff.

kevin-w: still seeing some 5xx spikes from a particular customer org id=org_9F3. Can we throttle or apply rate-limit rule?

maria_g: added a temporary per-org rate-limit on org_9F3 via console, 50% of usual.

kevin-w: ack. 5xx rate from that org dropped to near zero. Overall errors down.

alex_chung: ops-sre completed config bump on shards a-c (increased maxclients +10%). No restarts required. Accept_queue now ~120.

ops-sre: rolling restart avoided. We also evicted a few long-lived connections from old batch hosts.

pagerduty: PagerDuty update: Alert acknowledged by alex_chung at 6098765440, mitigated by routing and config changes.

maria_g: brief root cause hypothesis: traffic ramp triggered a small fleet of batch workers to hold long-lived Redis clients (leaked pipeline), causing accept queue and slowdowns. We'll run mem/proc analysis and correlate deploys.

alex_chung: creating incident summary and will escalate to eng-runtime for a postmortem if we confirm leak.

kevin-w: handing off to night oncall. I'll stay reachable for 10m. @kevin-w -> @raj_patel: please take ownership for monitoring and PM-tracking.

raj_patel: taking over. I'll keep the channel updated and run follow-up debug: heap dump scanning for leaked client pools + review batch job change logs between 11:00-11:40 UTC.

support-bot: Customer impact tally (provisional): 2 customers saw 5xx, ~300 requests degraded, no data loss. CS notified.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation cleared. Incident status -> mitigated.

kevin-w: thanks team. TL;DR: remedied by routing to fallback variants, temporary rate-limits, and increasing redis maxclients; follow-up PM for root cause (possible client leak).

alex_chung: filing follow-up ticket: https://redwood-internal/issues/RED-8842 "Redis accept queue - suspected client leak from batch workers" with action items: 1) postmortem, 2) add alert for client churn + long-lived pipeline commands, 3) tighten deploy gating for batch workers.

raj_patel: will post next update in 2 hours with debug artifacts.

maria_g: good catch on the EU ramp. Add a TODO to expand automated circuit-breaker so we don't need manual routing next time. :thumbsup:
